correctness.rationale: An unrestricted connected-edge determinant maximizer exists on the compact budget simplex. Reduced Laplacian is injective in complete-graph edge weights; strict concavity of log determinant therefore establishes full-edge uniqueness before imposing symmetry. The exact Laplacian eigenvalues are pa+qc with multiplicity p-1, qb+pc with multiplicity q-1, and (p+q)c once. Weighted Matrix–Tree gives c(pa+qc)^(p-1)(qb+pc)^(q-1). Homogeneity fixes multiplier (N-1)/B, and exact KKT per-expenditure return calculations establish all four mutually exclusive and exhaustive support cases including boundaries. A direct full-edge verifier passed 1,225 matrix determinant tests, 1,225 KKT/budget tests, 1,800 unrestricted feasible comparisons, and 30 full-space constrained optimizations. Finite tests are corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The contribution is the complete exact three-price support-region partition for unrestricted continuous conductance allocation on all two-community complete graphs. Existing cited work proves Matrix–Tree equivalence or supplies general numerical convex-design methods, rather than stating this all-size four-case classifier and the unequal-size two-stage support loss. Actual research-record semantic queries and targeted full primary-text comparisons identified no dominating theorem. This is a qualified priority assessment; generic convex solvability and unsuccessful searching alone are not evidence of novelty.

value.rationale: Two-community networks with different internal edge prices are a natural and nondegenerate D-optimal design family. The exact all-parameter allocation determines when each internal class should disappear, replacing generic numerical MAXDET solves with sharp linear support boundaries. The unequal-group same-price path produces two distinct structural changes, while balanced groups collapse simultaneously. It is a complete classification for infinite families and motivated network design choices, not an arbitrary finite table or minor numeric gain.
